description: Visually reviewed sprite groups. Numbers are items:N indexes, NOT gameplay item IDs. Actual exported sprite ID is N+2150.

notes.weapons/daggers: Start with items:80 for the ordinary RSC dagger silhouette and scale. Items:385 uses the same small-blade vocabulary with green poison coloring. Those two have handles toward lower left and tips toward upper right. Dark/glowing daggers 420/421 are larger, ornate exceptions with the opposite diagonal; do not inherit their size or angle unintentionally. Keep the short blade and small guard legible. The ordinary base is also reused for throwing knives.
notes.weapons/swords: Separate short, long, two-handed and curved blade silhouettes. Match the selected subtype's length within the canvas, not the biggest blade on the sheet. Rusty/broken examples are surface and damage references, not default proportions.
notes.weapons/staves: Use the plain staff for shaft thickness and diagonal placement; compare the orb-topped and decorated staffs for head size. Preserve clear separation between shaft and ornament. Broken staff is a damage reference only.
notes.weapons/bows: Keep the bow's arc, narrow limbs and string legible. Unstrung bows are included intentionally as shape references; do not infer a missing string is a rendering defect.
notes.ammunition/arrows: Bundles and single arrows are distinct compositions. Preserve the chosen count, direction and relative size; poison uses green accents rather than a glow cloud.
notes.ammunition/thrown: Darts have small heads and visible fletching. Throwing knives share the dagger base; follow the cross-reference rather than treating darts as knives.
notes.consumables/potions-and-bottles: Filled and empty conical vials provide the classic shape. Compare narrow-neck dye bottles, marked poison bottles and round potion variants separately. Keep the stopper and liquid silhouette readable at native size.
notes.materials/bones-and-monster-parts: Useful Slayer-component references: eye of newt, rat tail, unicorn horn, dragon scale, bones and tooth. Match one object's framing and shading; do not default to a pile when designing a single rare component.
notes.materials/hides-and-fur: Separate the smooth folded hide/leather shape from ragged furry silhouettes. Retain shading on the interior and readable irregular edges without adding a bright outline halo.
notes.jewelry/necklaces-and-amulets: Strung and unstrung variants differ in canvas occupancy. The thin chain or cord is part of the scale reference; keep it visible around the pendant rather than scaling only the ornament.
notes.materials/gems-and-crystals: Cut and uncut forms use different highlight geometry. Separate loose gems from pearls-in-shell and magical glow examples; borrow only the intended material treatment. Pink shards have inconsistent export bounds and are not a default canvas-size reference.
